title: MellinDuality: a Lean 4 formalization of Mellin duality for the band-parity companion
description:
Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying J. S. Farland, "Mellin duality for the band-parity companion, formalized in Lean" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23796262).

For an odd prime p and an odd character chi, the multiplier family C_chi(a) = sum over 0 < n < p/2 of chi(n)(-1)^(n + <a n^2>) has, at a = 1 and for the quartic character, the band-parity companion of a quartic L-value. Its Fourier transform over the characters is a product of two multiplier constants G(psi) = sum of psi(m)(-1)^m, which is 2(1 - 2 psi(2)) B_{1,psi} for odd psi and 0 for even psi, so the family is bilinear in first Bernoulli numbers.

The development proves: this Mellin duality and its inversion; the same statement for every even exponent n^(2m), with the collapse at the degenerate exponents; for the quartic character at p = 5 (mod 8): the coset lemma, the coset trace, the family means, the conjugate dynamics and the two second-moment identities; the decomposition of second-order products by coprime pairs, and Parseval's identity.

The development also proves the Bernoulli mean square: the sum over odd chi of |X_chi(a)|^2 is ((p-1)/2)^4. This is a corollary of the inversion and Parseval's identity over the odd characters, and no novelty is claimed for it.

The statements are in Challenge.lean. Lean's comparator checks them against the proofs, with the definition bodies compared, and the proofs are replayed in the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels. No sorry, no native_decide; standard axioms only. The changes in each version are described in the release notes on GitHub: github.com/jkfarland-bot/MellinDuality/releases.
notes: AI assistance: the Lean code in this record was drafted and repaired by Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, from the statements and proofs of the companion paper "Mellin duality for the band-parity companion, formalized in Lean" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23796262), and compiled locally with lake. Every proof is checked by the Lean kernel, and Comparator replays the solution against the statement file under the Lean, NanoDa and con-ron kernels. The author, Joseph S. Farland, chose the scope, directed the work, and is responsible for the contents. No external human reviewer has checked the formalization.
